obligations.text: The launch confinement and the witness sidecar each bind the self-test's probe socket in a fresh directory created under /tmp with mode 0700, whose path does not depend on the product home's path, and remove it when the self-test's owner is dropped.
The home sentinel stays inside the boundary entry, and the protected roots a confinement record names, and its digest, are the same as under spec 064.
A launch whose product home path is longer than the platform's socket path limit allows under spec 064 is no longer refused at the self-test's socket bind.

A launch with a product home whose path is over 100 bytes passes the self-test on macOS and Linux, the probe still reports unixDenied, and a confinement record's protected roots and digest equal the ones spec 064's tests record.

sectionHeadings: 3.3 What a long home now does
record.summary: Amends spec 064 section 3.3. The self-test's listening Unix socket moves from a directory under the product home's boundary entry to a private directory under /tmp, so its path no longer grows with the home's path and stays within the platform's socket path limit (104 bytes on macOS, 108 on Linux). The sentinel stays in boundary/, the protected roots and the confinement record are unchanged, and rule 6 of spec 004 section 3.18 still decides whether the probe's connect is refused.
record.title: The boundary self-test's probe socket lives under a short fixed directory, so a long home path cannot refuse a launch
